badges.description: This is a Porsche wheel center cap featuring their famous crest! The shield has a prancing black horse in the middle, surrounded by red and black stripes from the Stuttgart city coat of arms, and antlers from the Baden-Württemberg region of Germany!
badges.fun_fact: The prancing horse on the Porsche crest comes from the city of Stuttgart, Germany, where Porsche was founded - Stuttgart actually means 'stud farm' or horse stable in old German!

badges.description: This is a shiny chrome badge from the Audi 100 LS Automatic - a super cool European luxury car that was Audi's big debut into the premium car market! The 'LS' stood for 'Luxury Sport' and the Automatic badge meant it had an automatic transmission!
badges.fun_fact: The Audi 100 was secretly designed without the bosses at Volkswagen knowing - the engineers worked on it in secret and surprised everyone when it was revealed in 1968! Talk about a sneaky car!

badges.description: This is the famous galloping Mustang horse emblem that sits inside the grille of a Ford Mustang! The rectangular frame around the horse is part of the grille surround, making this a super cool piece of Mustang history!
badges.fun_fact: The Ford Mustang debuted at the 1964 World's Fair in New York, and over 22,000 were sold on the very first day! That galloping horse became one of the most famous car symbols EVER!

badges.description: This is the super cool Opel badge! It shows a lightning bolt cutting through a circle, which represents speed and energy. Opel is a famous German car brand that has been making awesome cars for over 160 years!
badges.fun_fact: The lightning bolt in the Opel logo is called a 'Blitz' in German, which literally means lightning! Opel used to make trucks called Blitz during World War II!

This is the famous Maserati Trident badge! The three-pronged spear called a trident comes from the Fountain of Neptune in Bologna, Italy, where Maserati was founded. The silver top half and blue bottom half make it super distinctive and elegant!
badges.fun_fact: The trident symbol was suggested by Maserati's brother Ettore, inspired by the giant Neptune statue in Bologna's city square - how cool is that?!

This super cool badge has a lightning bolt through a gear wheel on a red striped background, with four-pointed stars across the top! It's classic early 1960s Ford chrome — the kind of badge that made kids go WOW when these cars rolled by!
badges.fun_fact: In the early 1960s, Ford put lightning bolt and gear symbols on badges to show off their powerful engines — it was like telling the world 'this car is FAST and TOUGH!' The four-pointed stars were a Ford signature design used across many models in this era!

badges.description: This is a super cool vintage Datsun badge with a shiny chrome 'DS' monogram on a bright orange background! Datsun was the name Nissan used when they first brought Japanese cars to America, and this bold orange color makes it stand out like crazy!
badges.fun_fact: The name 'Datsun' originally came from 'DAT Motors' — and 'son of DAT' became 'Datson,' then 'Datsun!' Nissan eventually retired the Datsun name in the early 1980s, making these old badges real treasures to find!

badges.description: This is a center cap from a Raceline aftermarket wheel! It's the piece that snaps into the middle of the wheel to cover the lug nuts. The big bold 'R' logo and the RACELINE name going around the circle make it look super tough and sporty!
badges.fun_fact: Raceline wheels are super popular with off-road trucks and SUVs! They're built tough enough to handle desert racing, rock crawling, and mud bogging — serious extreme sports on four wheels!

This is the famous Chrysler Pentastar — a five-pointed star shape inside a laurel wreath, with red, white, and blue enamel colors! The laurel wreath around it means this was a really fancy, top-of-the-line badge used on premium Chrysler vehicles!
badges.fun_fact: The Pentastar logo was designed in 1962 and became one of the most recognized symbols in American car history — it appeared on millions of Chryslers, Dodges, and Plymouths for decades! The wreath version was reserved for the fanciest models!

badges.badge_name: Harley-Davidson Number One Skull Derby Cover
badges.description: This is a super cool Harley-Davidson motorcycle derby cover — the round chrome cap that sits on the engine! It features their famous '#1' logo with a skull hidden inside the number. This isn't a car badge — it's from a motorcycle engine!
badges.fun_fact: Harley-Davidson's '#1' logo dates back to 1969 when Cal Rayborn won the Daytona 200 race — Harley put the #1 on everything to celebrate, and fans loved it so much they never stopped! The skull version makes it extra tough-looking!

badges.description: This is the classic Land Rover badge — a shiny green oval with gold letters! Land Rovers are the ultimate adventure machines, built to climb mountains, cross rivers, and go places regular cars would never dare to go!
badges.fun_fact: Land Rover once tested their vehicles by driving them up a ski slope! The original Land Rover from 1948 was inspired by a Jeep, and the body was made of aluminum because steel was hard to get after World War II!

badges.description: This is the super cool Z Series badge from Nissan's legendary sports car lineup! That big bold Z with 'SERIES' written across it is one of the most iconic sports car logos ever made. It's machined aluminum with a dark background — totally awesome looking!
badges.fun_fact: The Nissan Z has been a sports car legend since 1969! The original 240Z was so popular it basically saved Nissan's entire American business. Car fans call it simply 'The Z' — no other car needs just one letter as its name!

badges.badge_name: Jaguar Growler Wheel Center Cap / Horn Button Badge
badges.description: This is the legendary Jaguar 'Growler' badge — a fierce snarling jaguar cat face surrounded by the word JAGUAR in chrome! This style was used on steering wheel centers, horn buttons, and hubcaps on classic Jaguars. It's totally old-school and super cool!
badges.fun_fact: Jaguar cars were originally called SS Cars, but after World War II the company changed the name to Jaguar because 'SS' had bad associations with the war. The growling cat face became one of the most iconic symbols in British car history!

badges.description: This is the super cool winged badge from a MINI Cooper! It has a round circle in the middle with 'MINI' written on it, and swooping wings on both sides — like it's ready to FLY! This chrome badge is usually found on the hood or trunk of the car.
badges.fun_fact: The original MINI was so tiny and brilliant that British spies used them in car chases! When BMW brought MINI back in 2001, they kept the cool retro style but added modern power — and this awesome winged badge!

badges.description: This is the famous 'E-TYPE' chrome script badge from one of the most beautiful cars EVER MADE! Enzo Ferrari himself called the E-Type 'the most beautiful car in the world' — and he built Ferraris! This shiny chrome badge would have sat on the back or side of this legendary British sports car.
badges.fun_fact: The Jaguar E-Type could go 150 mph when it came out in 1961, which was INSANE fast back then! It cost way less than a Ferrari but could keep up with one — which drove Ferrari totally crazy!

badges.description: This is a super cool chrome SAAB lettering badge! SAAB made cars that were totally different from everything else — quirky, unique, and beloved by people who liked thinking outside the box. This silver chrome badge would have lived on the trunk or body of a Swedish-made SAAB automobile!
badges.fun_fact: SAAB stands for Svenska Aeroplan AB — they started out building AIRPLANES before they ever made a single car! That's why SAAB fans say their cars are 'born from jets!' How awesome is that?

badges.description: This is a Saab badge featuring their famous Griffin — a mythical creature that's half eagle, half lion! The blue circle with the red and gold Griffin is one of the coolest car logos ever made. Saab was a Swedish car company that also made jet fighter planes!
badges.fun_fact: The Griffin on the Saab badge comes from the coat of arms of Scania, a region in Sweden. Saab started out building WARPLANES before they ever made a single car — how awesome is that?!

badges.description: This photo shows a person making a fun silly face with their hands up — not a car badge! No automotive emblems, logos, or hood ornaments are visible in this image.
badges.fun_fact: Car badges are usually made of chrome, plastic, or enamel and are found on the grille, trunk, or hood of a car — not on people making goofy faces!

badges.description: This is a classic Chevrolet dog dish hubcap — a smaller center hubcap that snaps onto steel wheels! The famous Chevy bowtie logo sits right in the middle on a blue background, surrounded by shiny chrome steel. These were super common on trucks and base-model cars back in the day!
badges.fun_fact: Dog dish hubcaps got their nickname because they look exactly like a dog's water bowl! Chevy used millions of these on their trucks and work vehicles throughout the 1970s and 80s. Some kids actually DID use old ones as dog dishes!

badges.description: This is a super old and cool Volvo badge from one of Sweden's most historic cars! It has the Volvo name in chrome script on a black bar, topped with the model number '444' and the classic Volvo iron symbol in red and chrome. This badge is ANCIENT by car standards!
badges.fun_fact: The Volvo 444 was Sweden's most popular car in the late 1940s and 1950s — and Volvo's name actually comes from Latin meaning 'I Roll!' The iron symbol (♂) on Volvo badges represents the Roman god Mars and the element iron, because Sweden was famous for making super strong steel!

badges.description: This is a super cool badge that combines TWO companies in one circle! On the left it says SAAB and on the right it says SCANIA, with a fierce red and gold Griffin creature in the middle. The Griffin is a mythical beast — half eagle, half lion — making it one of the most legendary animals ever put on a car badge!
badges.fun_fact: Saab originally stood for Svenska Aeroplan AB — meaning they made AIRPLANES before they made cars! That's why their engineers were so obsessed with making cars that felt like flying. Saab and Scania were one big Swedish company before they split apart!

badges.badge_name: Volvo Iron Mark Wheel Center Cap
badges.description: This is a Volvo wheel center cap featuring their famous Iron Mark logo — a circle with a diagonal arrow pointing up-right, which is actually the ancient symbol for iron! Volvo used it because Sweden is famous for making super strong steel!
badges.fun_fact: The Volvo logo is literally the chemical symbol for iron from ancient Rome — the same symbol used in science for the planet Mars! So every Volvo is secretly wearing a space symbol on its wheels!
